```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE,

```

# Overview

This pipeline processes PacBio HiFi LSU amplicon data (primers LROR/LR5, ~900 bp)
targeting arbuscular mycorrhizal fungi (AMF, Glomeromycota) from páramo plants
rhizosphere compartments.

**Key differences from Illumina 16S pipeline:**

1. No paired-end merging — HiFi reads are already full-length
2. Reads come in random orientation — must orient using primer detection
3. PacBio-specific error model (`PacBioErrfun`) and wider alignment band (`BAND_SIZE=32`)
4. AMF taxonomy via phylogenetic placement (Delavaux pipeline), not naive Bayes
5. Consider OTU clustering in addition to ASVs due to intra-genomic rDNA variation in AMF

# 1 Set paths and primers

```{r set-paths}
# R project containing this Rmd and LSU_metadata_updated.csv
project_path <- "~/Documents/CouradeauLab/paramos/Rhizosphere/Amplicons/Rhizosphere_Amplicon_Data_Analysis"

# Base path to the PacBio LSU run
base_path <- "~/Documents/CouradeauLab/paramos/Rhizosphere/Amplicons/LSU/data/r64404e_20250325_141946/1_C03"

# Input paths
metadata_path <- file.path(project_path, "LSU_metadata_updated.csv")
fastq_path <- file.path(base_path, "fastq_output")
seqtab_path <- file.path(base_path, "analysis_output", "seqtab_nochim.rds")

# Updated Delavaux V18 pipeline/reference directory
pipeline_path <- "~/Documents/CouradeauLab/paramos/Rhizosphere/Amplicons/LSU/AMF-LSU-Database-and-Pipeline2/2024_AMFPipeline/2024_AMFPipeline_ASV"

# New output directory. The previous analysis_output directory is not overwritten.
out_path <- file.path(base_path, "analysis_output_corrected")
dir.create(out_path, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

fig_dir <- file.path(out_path, "figures")
table_dir <- file.path(out_path, "tables")
phylo_dir <- file.path(out_path, "V18_phylogenetic_placement")
dir.create(fig_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
dir.create(table_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

# Command-line programs used for local V18 placement. The shell chunks inherit
# these values from the current R session, so paths do not need to be duplicated.
conda_path <- Sys.which("conda")
if (!nzchar(conda_path) && file.exists("/opt/anaconda3/bin/conda")) {
  conda_path <- "/opt/anaconda3/bin/conda"
}
AMF_CONDA_ENV <- "amf_v18_local"
Sys.setenv(
  AMF_CONDA_EXE = conda_path,
  AMF_CONDA_ENV = AMF_CONDA_ENV,
  LSU_PHYLO_DIR = path.expand(phylo_dir),
  LSU_OUT_DIR = path.expand(out_path)
)

# Workflow switches
RUN_DADA2 <- FALSE          # FALSE reuses seqtab_path
PREPARE_PHYLOGENY <- TRUE   # prepares the clean V18 placement directory
RUN_ANCOMBC2 <- FALSE       # enable only after reviewing AMF depth/coverage

FWD <- "ACCCGCTGAACTTAAGC"  # LR0R, gene-specific sequence
REV <- "TCCTGAGGGAAACTTCG"  # LR5, written 5' to 3'
M13_F <- "GTAAAACGACGGCCAGT"
M13_R <- "CAGGAAACAGCTATGAC"

# These cutoffs reproduce the main LR0R–LR5 length distribution already observed.
# Reinspect the length plots before changing them.
MIN_LEN <- 850L
MAX_LEN <- 1100L
MAX_EE <- 2

# Feature filtering used only for beta-diversity stability/sensitivity.
# The unfiltered AMF object is retained and exported.
MIN_TOTAL_READS_BETA <- 10L
MIN_PREVALENCE_BETA <- 2L
TARGET_COVERAGE <- 0.95

cat("Project:", project_path, "\n")
cat("LSU run:", base_path, "\n")
cat("Results:", out_path, "\n")
cat("Primers: LR0R / LR5\n")

cat("Forward primer (LROR):", FWD, "\n")
cat("Reverse primer (LR5):", REV, "\n")
cat("Expected amplicon range:", MIN_LEN, "-", MAX_LEN, "bp\n")
```
# 2 Metadata validation

```{r}
if (!file.exists(metadata_path)) stop("Metadata file not found: ", metadata_path)

meta <- readr::read_csv(metadata_path, show_col_types = FALSE, trim_ws = TRUE) %>%
  mutate(
    across(where(is.character), trimws),
    Compartment = Shortened_description
  )

required_columns <- c(
  "SampleID", "BioSample", "Host_code", "Plant_replicate", "Sample_name",
  "Host_Part", "Host_species", "Shortened_description", "Ecosite"
)

missing_columns <- setdiff(required_columns, names(meta))
if (length(missing_columns) > 0) {
  stop("Metadata is missing: ", paste(missing_columns, collapse = ", "))
}
if (anyDuplicated(meta$SampleID)) stop("SampleID values are not unique.")
if (anyNA(meta$SampleID) || any(meta$SampleID == "")) stop("Blank SampleID found.")

expected_parts <- c("BR", "BS", "SP", "Rh", "root", "stolon", "BG", "leaf", "AG")
unexpected_parts <- setdiff(unique(meta$Compartment), expected_parts)
if (length(unexpected_parts) > 0) {
  warning("Unexpected compartment values: ", paste(unexpected_parts, collapse = ", "))
}

# In this metadata, Host_Part is a composite label such as Espeletia_BR, while
# Shortened_description contains the actual compartment code used in analyses.
expected_host_part <- paste(meta$Host_species, meta$Compartment, sep = "_")
if (any(meta$Host_Part != expected_host_part)) {
  warning("Host_Part is inconsistent with Host_species + Shortened_description.")
}

# A host code should map to one host genus and vice versa in this dataset.
code_audit <- meta %>%
  distinct(Host_species, Host_code) %>%
  add_count(Host_species, name = "codes_per_host") %>%
  arrange(desc(codes_per_host), Host_species, Host_code)
if (any(code_audit$codes_per_host > 1)) {
  warning(
    "A host genus maps to more than one Host_code. Inspect code_audit and ",
    "confirm every mapping before continuing."
  )
}

design_table <- meta %>%
  count(Host_species, Compartment, Ecosite, name = "n") %>%
  arrange(Host_species, Compartment)

knitr::kable(code_audit, caption = "Host-code audit")
knitr::kable(design_table, caption = "LSU sampling design")

write.csv(design_table, file.path(table_dir, "LSU_sampling_design.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
```
```{r design-plot}
part_order <- expected_parts
meta <- meta %>%
  mutate(
    Compartment = factor(Compartment, levels = part_order),
    Host_species = factor(Host_species),
    Ecosite = factor(Ecosite)
  )

p_design <- design_table %>%
  mutate(
    Compartment = factor(Compartment, levels = part_order),
    Host_species = factor(Host_species, levels = levels(meta$Host_species))
  ) %>%
  ggplot(aes(Compartment, Host_species, fill = n)) +
  geom_tile(color = "white", linewidth = 0.6) +
  geom_text(aes(label = n), size = 4) +
  scale_fill_viridis_c(option = "C", begin = 0.15, end = 0.9) +
  labs(x = "Compartment or organ", y = "Host genus", fill = "Samples",
       title = "LSU sampling design") +
  theme(panel.grid = element_blank())

p_design
ggsave(file.path(fig_dir, "LSU_sampling_design.pdf"), p_design, width = 8, height = 4.8)
```
```{r ecosite-confounding}
host_ecosite <- table(meta$Host_species, meta$Ecosite)
host_ecosite

ecosites_per_host <- rowSums(host_ecosite > 0)
if (all(ecosites_per_host == 1)) {
  cat("Ecosite tests skipped: each host genus occurs in only one ecosite category.\n")
}
```

# 3. FASTQ audit

```{r fastq-audit}
fastq_files <- sort(list.files(
  fastq_path, pattern = "\\.fastq(?:\\.gz)?$", full.names = TRUE
))
sample_names <- sub("\\.fastq(?:\\.gz)?$", "", basename(fastq_files))

if (length(fastq_files) == 0) stop("No FASTQ files found in: ", fastq_path)
if (anyDuplicated(sample_names)) stop("Duplicate FASTQ sample names detected.")

fastq_metadata_audit <- tibble(
  issue = c("FASTQ absent from metadata", "Metadata absent from FASTQ"),
  samples = c(
    paste(setdiff(sample_names, as.character(meta$SampleID)), collapse = "; "),
    paste(setdiff(as.character(meta$SampleID), sample_names), collapse = "; ")
  )
)
knitr::kable(fastq_metadata_audit)

if (!setequal(sample_names, as.character(meta$SampleID))) {
  stop("FASTQ and metadata SampleID sets differ. Resolve the audit table above.")
}

cat(length(fastq_files), "FASTQs match", nrow(meta), "metadata rows.\n")
```

```{r primer-audit, eval=RUN_DADA2}
primer_hits <- function(primer, files) {
  vapply(files, function(f) {
    fq <- readFastq(f)
    sum(vcountPattern(primer, sread(fq), fixed = FALSE) > 0)
  }, numeric(1))
}

primer_qc <- tibble(
  SampleID = sample_names,
  reads = vapply(fastq_files, function(f) length(readFastq(f)), numeric(1)),
  LR0R = primer_hits(FWD, fastq_files),
  LR5_rc = primer_hits(rc(REV), fastq_files),
  residual_M13_F = primer_hits(M13_F, fastq_files),
  residual_M13_R_rc = primer_hits(rc(M13_R), fastq_files)
) %>%
  mutate(across(LR0R:residual_M13_R_rc, ~ .x / reads, .names = "prop_{.col}"))

write.csv(primer_qc, file.path(table_dir, "primer_audit.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
summary(select(primer_qc, starts_with("prop_")))
```

# 4. PacBio DADA2 denoising

The existing denoised sequence table can be reused because the principal error
was downstream AMF classification, not ASV inference. Set `RUN_DADA2 <- TRUE`
in the paths chunk only when rebuilding from FASTQ.

```{r remove-primers, eval=RUN_DADA2}
noprimer_dir <- file.path(out_path, "fastq_noprimers")
filtered_dir <- file.path(out_path, "fastq_filtered")
dir.create(noprimer_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
dir.create(filtered_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

noprimer_files <- file.path(
  noprimer_dir, paste0(sample_names, "_noprimer.fastq.gz")
)
names(fastq_files) <- names(noprimer_files) <- sample_names

# Reads occur in either orientation. For forward-oriented amplicons, the LR5
# sequence present in the read is the reverse complement of the primer supplied
# by the laboratory.
primer_summary <- removePrimers(
  fn = fastq_files,
  fout = noprimer_files,
  primer.fwd = FWD,
  primer.rev = rc(REV),
  orient = TRUE,
  max.mismatch = 2,
  allow.indels = TRUE,
  verbose = TRUE
)

write.csv(primer_summary, file.path(table_dir, "primer_removal_tracking.csv"))
primer_summary
```

```{r post-primer-lengths, eval=RUN_DADA2}
length_sample <- width(sread(readFastq(noprimer_files[[1]])))

qplot(length_sample, bins = 80) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = c(MIN_LEN, MAX_LEN), linetype = "dashed") +
  labs(x = "Length after primer removal (bp)", y = "Reads",
       title = "Post-primer amplicon lengths: first sample")
```

```{r filter-denoise, eval=RUN_DADA2}
filtered_files <- file.path(
  filtered_dir, paste0(sample_names, "_filtered.fastq.gz")
)
names(filtered_files) <- sample_names

filter_summary <- filterAndTrim(
  fwd = noprimer_files,
  filt = filtered_files,
  minLen = MIN_LEN,
  maxLen = MAX_LEN,
  maxN = 0,
  maxEE = MAX_EE,
  minQ = 3,
  rm.phix = FALSE,
  compress = TRUE,
  multithread = TRUE,
  verbose = TRUE
)

if (any(filter_summary[, "reads.out"] == 0)) {
  stop("At least one sample has zero reads after filtering; inspect filter_summary.")
}

err <- learnErrors(
  filtered_files,
  errorEstimationFunction = PacBioErrfun,
  BAND_SIZE = 32,
  multithread = TRUE,
  randomize = TRUE,
  verbose = TRUE
)
saveRDS(err, file.path(out_path, "PacBio_error_model.rds"))
plotErrors(err, nominalQ = TRUE)

derep <- derepFastq(filtered_files, verbose = TRUE)
names(derep) <- sample_names

dada_out <- dada(
  derep,
  err = err,
  BAND_SIZE = 32,
  pool = "pseudo",
  multithread = TRUE
)

seqtab_sequence_names <- makeSequenceTable(dada_out)
seqtab_sequence_names <- removeBimeraDenovo(
  seqtab_sequence_names,
  method = "consensus",
  multithread = TRUE,
  verbose = TRUE
)

getN <- function(x) sum(getUniques(x))
tracking <- tibble(
  SampleID = sample_names,
  input = primer_summary[, 1],
  primer_oriented = primer_summary[, 2],
  filtered = filter_summary[, "reads.out"],
  denoised = vapply(dada_out, getN, numeric(1)),
  nonchim = rowSums(seqtab_sequence_names)
)

write.csv(tracking, file.path(table_dir, "DADA2_read_tracking.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
saveRDS(seqtab_sequence_names, file.path(out_path, "seqtab_nochim_sequences.rds"))
```

```{r load-seqtab}
if (RUN_DADA2) {
  seqtab_sequence_names <- readRDS(
    file.path(out_path, "seqtab_nochim_sequences.rds")
  )
} else {
  if (!file.exists(seqtab_path)) {
    stop("Existing DADA2 sequence table not found: ", seqtab_path)
  }
  seqtab_sequence_names <- readRDS(seqtab_path)
}

if (!is.matrix(seqtab_sequence_names)) {
  seqtab_sequence_names <- as.matrix(seqtab_sequence_names)
}
if (!setequal(rownames(seqtab_sequence_names), as.character(meta$SampleID))) {
  stop("DADA2 table sample names do not match LSU metadata.")
}

# Reorder once, explicitly, to the metadata.
seqtab_sequence_names <- seqtab_sequence_names[as.character(meta$SampleID), , drop = FALSE]
asv_sequences <- colnames(seqtab_sequence_names)

if (!all(grepl("^[ACGTN]+$", asv_sequences))) {
  stop("Expected DNA sequences as columns of seqtab_nochim.rds.")
}

asv_ids <- paste0("ASV", seq_along(asv_sequences))
seqtab_ids <- seqtab_sequence_names
colnames(seqtab_ids) <- asv_ids

asv_map <- tibble(
  ASV_ID = asv_ids,
  Sequence = asv_sequences,
  Length = nchar(asv_sequences),
  Total_reads = colSums(seqtab_ids),
  Prevalence = colSums(seqtab_ids > 0)
)

write.csv(asv_map, file.path(table_dir, "LSU_ASV_ID_mapping.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
saveRDS(seqtab_ids, file.path(out_path, "seqtab_nochim_ASV_IDs.rds"))

cat(nrow(seqtab_ids), "samples;", ncol(seqtab_ids), "non-chimeric ASVs\n")
summary(asv_map$Length)
```

```{r export-asvs}
asv_set <- DNAStringSet(asv_map$Sequence)
names(asv_set) <- asv_map$ASV_ID
writeXStringSet(asv_set, file.path(out_path, "LSU_ASVs.fasta"), width = 10000)

count_export <- as.data.frame(t(seqtab_ids), check.names = FALSE) %>%
  rownames_to_column("X.ASV.ID")
readr::write_tsv(count_export, file.path(out_path, "LSU_ASV_counts.tsv"))
```

# 5. AMF identification with the V18 backbone

## 5.1 Prepare a clean placement workspace

```{r prepare-v18, eval=PREPARE_PHYLOGENY}
needed_v18_files <- c(
  "V18_LSUDB_052025.fasta",
  "V18_LSUDB_052025_AMFONLY.fasta",
  "Root_V18_LSUDB_052025.newick",
  "AMFcladesExtract.R",
  "AMFcladeTaxonomy.R"
)

missing_v18 <- needed_v18_files[
  !file.exists(file.path(pipeline_path, needed_v18_files))
]
if (length(missing_v18) > 0) {
  stop("Missing V18 pipeline assets: ", paste(missing_v18, collapse = ", "))
}

dir.create(phylo_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
dir.create(file.path(phylo_dir, "RAxMLfiles"), showWarnings = FALSE)
dir.create(file.path(phylo_dir, "cladeOutputs"), showWarnings = FALSE)
dir.create(file.path(phylo_dir, "batches"), showWarnings = FALSE)

file.copy(
  file.path(pipeline_path, needed_v18_files),
  file.path(phylo_dir, needed_v18_files),
  overwrite = TRUE
)
file.copy(
  file.path(out_path, "LSU_ASVs.fasta"),
  file.path(phylo_dir, "ASVrepseqs_clean.fasta"),
  overwrite = TRUE
)
file.copy(
  file.path(out_path, "LSU_ASV_counts.tsv"),
  file.path(phylo_dir, "ASVtable_clean.tsv"),
  overwrite = TRUE
)

cat("V18 placement workspace prepared at:\n", phylo_dir, "\n")
```

## 5.2 Permissive BLAST pre-screen

```{bash v18-prescreen, eval=FALSE}
set -euo pipefail

: "${AMF_CONDA_EXE:?Run the R paths chunk first}"
: "${AMF_CONDA_ENV:?Run the R paths chunk first}"
: "${LSU_PHYLO_DIR:?Run the R paths chunk first}"
cd "${LSU_PHYLO_DIR}"

# Remove results derived from the earlier AMF-only screen so they cannot be
# reused accidentally before the competitive screen has been processed.
rm -f \
  candidate_ASV_ids.txt \
  V18_competitive_blast.tsv \
  V18_competitive_blast_audit.tsv \
  ASVrepseqs_clean_BLAST.fasta \
  ASVtable_clean_BLASTonly.tsv \
  V18_plus_candidates_aligned.fasta

"${AMF_CONDA_EXE}" run --no-capture-output -n "${AMF_CONDA_ENV}" makeblastdb \
  -in V18_LSUDB_052025.fasta \
  -dbtype nucl \
  -out V18_LSUDB_052025_full

"${AMF_CONDA_EXE}" run --no-capture-output -n "${AMF_CONDA_ENV}" blastn \
  -query ASVrepseqs_clean.fasta \
  -db V18_LSUDB_052025_full \
  -evalue 1e-3 \
  -max_target_seqs 5 \
  -num_threads 10 \
  -outfmt '6 qseqid sseqid pident length qlen evalue bitscore' \
  -out V18_competitive_blast.tsv

test -s V18_competitive_blast.tsv || {
  echo "ERROR: competitive V18 BLAST produced no hits." >&2
  exit 1
}
wc -l V18_competitive_blast.tsv
```

## 5.3 Create candidate files

Run this chunk after `V18_competitive_blast.tsv` exists. The complete audit
table is retained so every inclusion and exclusion can be reviewed.

```{r subset-v18-candidates}
blast_file <- file.path(phylo_dir, "V18_competitive_blast.tsv")
candidate_file <- file.path(phylo_dir, "candidate_ASV_ids.txt")

if (file.exists(blast_file)) {
  blast_hits <- readr::read_tsv(
    blast_file,
    col_names = c(
      "ASV_ID", "Reference_ID", "Percent_identity", "Alignment_length",
      "Query_length", "Evalue", "Bitscore"
    ),
    show_col_types = FALSE
  )

  amf_reference_ids <- names(readDNAStringSet(
    file.path(phylo_dir, "V18_LSUDB_052025_AMFONLY.fasta")
  ))

  blast_hits <- blast_hits %>%
    mutate(
      Query_coverage = Alignment_length / Query_length,
      AMF_reference = Reference_ID %in% amf_reference_ids
    )

  best_amf <- blast_hits %>%
    filter(AMF_reference) %>%
    arrange(ASV_ID, desc(Bitscore), Evalue, desc(Query_coverage)) %>%
    distinct(ASV_ID, .keep_all = TRUE) %>%
    transmute(
      ASV_ID,
      AMF_reference_ID = Reference_ID,
      AMF_percent_identity = Percent_identity,
      AMF_alignment_length = Alignment_length,
      Query_length,
      AMF_query_coverage = Query_coverage,
      AMF_evalue = Evalue,
      AMF_bitscore = Bitscore
    )

  best_outgroup <- blast_hits %>%
    filter(!AMF_reference) %>%
    arrange(ASV_ID, desc(Bitscore), Evalue, desc(Query_coverage)) %>%
    distinct(ASV_ID, .keep_all = TRUE) %>%
    transmute(
      ASV_ID,
      Outgroup_reference_ID = Reference_ID,
      Outgroup_bitscore = Bitscore
    )

  blast_audit <- full_join(best_amf, best_outgroup, by = "ASV_ID") %>%
    mutate(
      Candidate_for_placement =
        !is.na(AMF_bitscore) &
        AMF_query_coverage >= 0.50 &
        (is.na(Outgroup_bitscore) | AMF_bitscore >= Outgroup_bitscore)
    ) %>%
    arrange(desc(Candidate_for_placement), ASV_ID)

  readr::write_tsv(
    blast_audit,
    file.path(phylo_dir, "V18_competitive_blast_audit.tsv")
  )

  candidate_ids <- blast_audit %>%
    filter(Candidate_for_placement) %>%
    pull(ASV_ID) %>%
    intersect(asv_ids)

  if (length(candidate_ids) == 0) {
    stop("Competitive V18 BLAST pre-screen returned no candidate ASVs.")
  }
  writeLines(candidate_ids, candidate_file)

  candidate_set <- asv_set[candidate_ids]
  writeXStringSet(
    candidate_set,
    file.path(phylo_dir, "ASVrepseqs_clean_BLAST.fasta"),
    width = 10000
  )

  candidate_counts <- count_export %>% filter(X.ASV.ID %in% candidate_ids)
  readr::write_tsv(
    candidate_counts,
    file.path(phylo_dir, "ASVtable_clean_BLASTonly.tsv")
  )
  cat(length(candidate_ids), "candidate ASVs prepared for placement.\n")
  print(blast_audit %>% count(Candidate_for_placement))
} else {
  cat("V18_competitive_blast.tsv is not present yet; run section 5.2 first.\n")
}
```

## 5.4 Reference-coordinate alignment

This uses V18 as the alignment reference and drops LR5-region overhangs that are
not represented in V18. It therefore compares homologous LSU positions while
retaining the LR0R–LR5 reads for ASV inference and archiving.

```{bash v18-alignment, eval=FALSE}
set -euo pipefail

: "${AMF_CONDA_EXE:?Run the R paths chunk first}"
: "${AMF_CONDA_ENV:?Run the R paths chunk first}"
: "${LSU_PHYLO_DIR:?Run the R paths chunk first}"
cd "${LSU_PHYLO_DIR}"

"${AMF_CONDA_EXE}" run --no-capture-output -n "${AMF_CONDA_ENV}" mafft \
  --auto --thread -1 \
  V18_LSUDB_052025.fasta \
  > V18_LSUDB_052025_aligned.fasta

"${AMF_CONDA_EXE}" run --no-capture-output -n "${AMF_CONDA_ENV}" mafft \
  --addfragments ASVrepseqs_clean_BLAST.fasta \
  --keeplength --thread -1 \
  V18_LSUDB_052025_aligned.fasta \
  > V18_plus_candidates_aligned.fasta
```

## 5.5 Split aligned ASVs into constrained-tree batches

```{r make-placement-batches}
aligned_file <- file.path(phylo_dir, "V18_plus_candidates_aligned.fasta")
backbone_file <- file.path(phylo_dir, "Root_V18_LSUDB_052025.newick")

if (file.exists(aligned_file)) {
  aligned <- readDNAStringSet(aligned_file)
  names(aligned) <- trimws(names(aligned))

if (anyDuplicated(names(aligned))) {
  stop("Duplicate sequence identifiers after trimming FASTA headers.")
}
  backbone <- read.tree(backbone_file)

  missing_backbone_tips <- setdiff(backbone$tip.label, names(aligned))
  if (length(missing_backbone_tips) > 0) {
    stop(
      "Aligned FASTA is missing backbone tips; first missing tip: ",
      missing_backbone_tips[[1]]
    )
  }

  reference_aligned <- aligned[backbone$tip.label]
  query_aligned <- aligned[grepl("^ASV[0-9]+$", names(aligned))]
  if (length(query_aligned) == 0) stop("No aligned ASV sequences found.")

  batch_size <- 15L  # follows the validated V18 pipeline's placement batch size
  batch_id <- ceiling(seq_along(query_aligned) / batch_size)
  batch_dir <- file.path(phylo_dir, "batches")
  old_batches <- list.files(batch_dir, pattern = "^batch_[0-9]+\\.fasta$", full.names = TRUE)
  if (length(old_batches) > 0) file.remove(old_batches)

  for (i in sort(unique(batch_id))) {
    batch_queries <- query_aligned[batch_id == i]
    writeXStringSet(
      c(reference_aligned, batch_queries),
      file.path(batch_dir, sprintf("batch_%04d.fasta", i)),
      width = 10000
    )
  }

  cat(length(unique(batch_id)), "tree batches created for", length(query_aligned), "ASVs.\n")
} else {
  cat("Aligned candidate file not found; run section 5.4, then rerun this chunk.\n")
}
```

## 5.6 Constrained placement and V18 clade extraction

The command below uses classic RAxML because the V18 extraction scripts expect
its tree filenames. It processes batches sequentially and gives each tree eight
threads. This can take many hours or days on a laptop, depending on how many
candidate ASVs pass BLAST. Keep the Mac connected to power and prevent system
sleep while this chunk is running. The generic threaded executable is used
instead of the AVX2 build because this Mac has Apple Silicon.

```{bash v18-constrained-trees, eval=FALSE}
set -euo pipefail

: "${AMF_CONDA_EXE:?Run the R paths chunk first}"
: "${AMF_CONDA_ENV:?Run the R paths chunk first}"
: "${LSU_PHYLO_DIR:?Run the R paths chunk first}"
cd "${LSU_PHYLO_DIR}"

mkdir -p RAxMLfiles cladeOutputs

RAXML_BIN=$("${AMF_CONDA_EXE}" run -n "${AMF_CONDA_ENV}" sh -c \
  'command -v raxmlHPC-PTHREADS || command -v raxmlHPC-PTHREADS-SSE3 || command -v raxmlHPC')
test -n "${RAXML_BIN}" || {
  echo "ERROR: no non-AVX classic RAxML executable was found." >&2
  exit 1
}

shopt -s nullglob
alignments=(batches/batch_*.fasta)
test "${#alignments[@]}" -gt 0 || {
  echo "ERROR: no placement batches were found; run section 5.5 first." >&2
  exit 1
}

for alignment in "${alignments[@]}"; do
  batch_name=$(basename "$alignment" .fasta)
  run_name="${batch_name}_AMFtree.ENVbackbone"
  best_tree="RAxMLfiles/RAxML_bestTree.${run_name}"

  if [[ -s "${best_tree}" ]]; then
    echo "Skipping completed ${batch_name}"
    continue
  fi

  # Remove only incomplete outputs for this exact batch before retrying it.
  rm -f \
    "RAxMLfiles/RAxML_info.${run_name}" \
    "RAxMLfiles/RAxML_log.${run_name}" \
    "RAxMLfiles/RAxML_result.${run_name}" \
    "RAxMLfiles/RAxML_parsimonyTree.${run_name}"

  "${AMF_CONDA_EXE}" run --no-capture-output -n "${AMF_CONDA_ENV}" \
    "${RAXML_BIN}" \
    -f d \
    -m GTRGAMMA \
    -p 1723 \
    -N 100 \
    -r Root_V18_LSUDB_052025.newick \
    -s "$alignment" \
    -n "${run_name}" \
    -T 8 \
    -w "$(pwd)/RAxMLfiles"
done
```

package library as the notebook:

# 6. Import phylogenetically validated AMF ASVs

```{r v18-taxonomy-checkpoint}
taxonomy_file <- file.path(phylo_dir, "ASVtable_clean_AMFonly_taxonomy.tsv")

if (!file.exists(taxonomy_file)) {
  cat(
    "V18 taxonomy output is not present yet. The notebook will stop cleanly here.\n",
    "Complete sections 5.2–5.6, then knit again.\n"
  )
  knitr::knit_exit()
}
```

```{r import-v18-taxonomy}
tax_v18 <- readr::read_tsv(taxonomy_file, show_col_types = FALSE)
id_candidates <- intersect(
  c("X.ASV.ID", "ASV_ID", "ASV.ID", "#ASV ID"), names(tax_v18)
)
if (length(id_candidates) != 1) stop("Could not identify the ASV ID column in V18 taxonomy.")
names(tax_v18)[names(tax_v18) == id_candidates] <- "ASV_ID"

names(tax_v18) <- sub("^phylum$", "Phylum", names(tax_v18), ignore.case = TRUE)
names(tax_v18) <- sub("^family$", "Family", names(tax_v18), ignore.case = TRUE)
names(tax_v18) <- sub("^genus$", "Genus", names(tax_v18), ignore.case = TRUE)

if (!all(c("ASV_ID", "Phylum", "Family", "Genus") %in% names(tax_v18))) {
  stop("V18 taxonomy must contain ASV_ID, Phylum, Family, and Genus.")
}
if (anyDuplicated(tax_v18$ASV_ID)) stop("Duplicate ASV IDs in V18 taxonomy output.")

tax_v18 <- tax_v18 %>%
  transmute(
    ASV_ID,
    Kingdom = "Fungi",
    Phylum = replace_na(Phylum, "Glomeromycota_unresolved"),
    Family = replace_na(Family, "Unclassified_Glomeromycota"),
    Genus = replace_na(Genus, "Unclassified_Glomeromycota")
  )

amf_ids <- intersect(tax_v18$ASV_ID, colnames(seqtab_ids))
if (length(amf_ids) == 0) stop("No V18 AMF IDs match the DADA2 count table.")

amf_counts <- seqtab_ids[, amf_ids, drop = FALSE]
tax_v18 <- tax_v18 %>% filter(ASV_ID %in% amf_ids) %>% arrange(match(ASV_ID, amf_ids))

tax_matrix <- tax_v18 %>%
  column_to_rownames("ASV_ID") %>%
  as.matrix()

meta_ps <- meta %>% as.data.frame()
rownames(meta_ps) <- as.character(meta_ps$SampleID)

ps_amf_all <- phyloseq(
  otu_table(t(amf_counts), taxa_are_rows = TRUE),
  tax_table(tax_matrix),
  sample_data(meta_ps)
)

# Only zero-AMF samples are removed automatically. No arbitrary read threshold is
# imposed. Coverage and sensitivity diagnostics below guide any later exclusion.
zero_amf_samples <- sample_names(ps_amf_all)[sample_sums(ps_amf_all) == 0]
ps_amf <- prune_samples(sample_sums(ps_amf_all) > 0, ps_amf_all)
ps_amf <- prune_taxa(taxa_sums(ps_amf) > 0, ps_amf)

saveRDS(ps_amf_all, file.path(out_path, "ps_amf_V18_all_samples.rds"))
saveRDS(ps_amf, file.path(out_path, "ps_amf_V18_nonzero_samples.rds"))

cat("Phylogenetically validated AMF ASVs:", ntaxa(ps_amf_all), "\n")
cat("Samples with AMF reads:", nsamples(ps_amf), "of", nsamples(ps_amf_all), "\n")
if (length(zero_amf_samples) > 0) print(zero_amf_samples)
```

# 7. Sequencing-depth and coverage diagnostics

```{r depth-coverage}
amf_matrix <- as(otu_table(ps_amf), "matrix")
if (taxa_are_rows(ps_amf)) amf_matrix <- t(amf_matrix)

goods_coverage <- apply(amf_matrix, 1, function(x) {
  if (sum(x) == 0) return(NA_real_)
  1 - sum(x == 1) / sum(x)
})

depth_df <- data.frame(sample_data(ps_amf)) %>%
  rownames_to_column("SampleID_join") %>%
  mutate(
    AMF_reads = sample_sums(ps_amf)[SampleID_join],
    Observed_ASVs = rowSums(amf_matrix > 0)[SampleID_join],
    Goods_coverage = goods_coverage[SampleID_join]
  )

write.csv(depth_df, file.path(table_dir, "AMF_sample_depth_and_coverage.csv"), row.names = FALSE)

p_depth <- ggplot(depth_df, aes(Compartment, AMF_reads, color = Host_species)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 1, color = "grey75") +
  geom_jitter(width = 0.14, height = 0, size = 2.5, alpha = 0.85) +
  scale_y_log10(labels = scales::comma) +
  labs(x = "Compartment or organ", y = "Phylogenetically validated AMF reads",
       color = "Host genus", title = "AMF library size") +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))

p_cov <- ggplot(depth_df, aes(Compartment, Goods_coverage, color = Host_species)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = TARGET_COVERAGE, linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_jitter(width = 0.14, height = 0, size = 2.5, alpha = 0.85) +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0, 1)) +
  labs(x = "Compartment or organ", y = "Good's coverage",
       color = "Host genus", title = "Per-sample sampling coverage") +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))

p_depth + p_cov
ggsave(file.path(fig_dir, "AMF_depth_and_coverage.pdf"),
       p_depth + p_cov, width = 13, height = 5.5)
```

Good's coverage is a diagnostic, not a substitute for coverage-based diversity
estimation. Samples with low AMF read counts or coverage should be reported and
examined in sensitivity analyses instead of being removed with an unexplained
10,000- or 15,000-read cutoff.

# 9. Alpha diversity

AMF rDNA can show intragenomic variation, so ASV richness is not interpreted as
a literal species count. The preferred alpha-diversity panel uses Hill numbers
standardized to equal sample coverage. Install `iNEXT` to run this section.

```{r coverage-based-alpha}
alpha_estimates <- NULL

if (requireNamespace("iNEXT", quietly = TRUE)) {
  abundance_list <- lapply(seq_len(nrow(amf_matrix)), function(i) {
    x <- amf_matrix[i, ]
    unname(x[x > 0])
  })
  names(abundance_list) <- rownames(amf_matrix)

  alpha_estimates <- iNEXT::estimateD(
    abundance_list,
    q = c(0, 1, 2),
    datatype = "abundance",
    base = "coverage",
    level = TARGET_COVERAGE,
    conf = 0.95
  ) %>%
    rename(SampleID_join = Assemblage) %>%
    left_join(
      depth_df %>% select(SampleID_join, Host_species, Compartment, Ecosite),
      by = "SampleID_join"
    ) %>%
    mutate(
      Diversity = recode(as.character(Order.q),
                         `0` = "Richness", `1` = "Shannon diversity",
                         `2` = "Simpson diversity"),
      Compartment = factor(Compartment, levels = part_order)
    )

  write.csv(alpha_estimates, file.path(table_dir, "AMF_Hill_diversity_coverage_095.csv"),
            row.names = FALSE)

  p_alpha <- ggplot(alpha_estimates, aes(Compartment, qD, color = Host_species)) +
    geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = qD.LCL, ymax = qD.UCL), width = 0, alpha = 0.5) +
    geom_jitter(width = 0.13, size = 2.3) +
    facet_wrap(~ Diversity, scales = "free_y") +
    labs(x = "Compartment or organ", y = "Coverage-standardized Hill diversity",
         color = "Host genus", title = "AMF alpha diversity at 95% coverage") +
    theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))

  p_alpha
  ggsave(file.path(fig_dir, "AMF_coverage_standardized_alpha.pdf"),
         p_alpha, width = 13, height = 5)
} else {
  cat("Install iNEXT to calculate coverage-standardized Hill diversity.\n")
}
```

With two or three independent samples per host–compartment cell, formal
within-host alpha-diversity tests have low power and discrete P-values. Report
estimates and intervals as primary; treat the following tests as exploratory.

```{r alpha-tests}
alpha_tests <- NULL
if (!is.null(alpha_estimates)) {
  alpha_tests <- alpha_estimates %>%
    group_by(Host_species, Diversity) %>%
    filter(n_distinct(Compartment) >= 2) %>%
    summarise(
      n = n(),
      groups = n_distinct(Compartment),
      p = if (n_distinct(Compartment) >= 2) kruskal.test(qD ~ Compartment)$p.value else NA_real_,
      .groups = "drop"
    ) %>%
    mutate(q = p.adjust(p, method = "BH"))

  write.csv(alpha_tests, file.path(table_dir, "AMF_alpha_within_host_tests.csv"),
            row.names = FALSE)
  knitr::kable(alpha_tests, digits = 3)
}
```

# 10. Beta diversity

Bray–Curtis on proportional counts and Aitchison distance on centered log-ratio
transformed counts are shown. Neither requires rarefaction. Low-information ASVs
are filtered only for beta-diversity stability, and the thresholds are recorded
at the top of the notebook.

```{r beta-objects}
beta_keep <- taxa_sums(ps_amf) >= MIN_TOTAL_READS_BETA &
  apply(as(otu_table(ps_amf), "matrix"), 1, function(x) sum(x > 0)) >= MIN_PREVALENCE_BETA

ps_beta <- prune_taxa(beta_keep, ps_amf)
beta_counts <- as(otu_table(ps_beta), "matrix")
if (taxa_are_rows(ps_beta)) beta_counts <- t(beta_counts)

beta_rel <- sweep(beta_counts, 1, rowSums(beta_counts), "/")
bray <- vegdist(beta_rel, method = "bray")

log_counts <- log(beta_counts + 0.5)
clr_counts <- log_counts - rowMeans(log_counts)
aitchison <- dist(clr_counts, method = "euclidean")

meta_beta <- data.frame(sample_data(ps_beta))
meta_beta <- meta_beta[rownames(beta_counts), , drop = FALSE]

pcoa_frame <- function(distance_object, metadata, distance_label) {
  ord <- cmdscale(distance_object, k = 2, eig = TRUE, add = TRUE)
  variance <- ord$eig[ord$eig > 0] / sum(ord$eig[ord$eig > 0]) * 100
  out <- as.data.frame(ord$points)
  names(out) <- c("Axis1", "Axis2")
  out$SampleID_join <- rownames(out)
  out <- bind_cols(out, metadata[rownames(out), , drop = FALSE])
  attr(out, "axis_labels") <- c(
    paste0("PCoA1 (", round(variance[1], 1), "%)"),
    paste0("PCoA2 (", round(variance[2], 1), "%)")
  )
  attr(out, "distance_label") <- distance_label
  out
}

bray_scores <- pcoa_frame(bray, meta_beta, "Bray–Curtis")
aitchison_scores <- pcoa_frame(aitchison, meta_beta, "Aitchison")
```

```{r beta-plots}
plot_pcoa <- function(scores) {
  axis_labels <- attr(scores, "axis_labels")
  distance_label <- attr(scores, "distance_label")

  ggplot(scores, aes(Axis1, Axis2, color = Compartment, shape = Host_species)) +
    geom_point(size = 3, alpha = 0.85) +
    facet_wrap(~ Host_species, scales = "free") +
    labs(x = axis_labels[1], y = axis_labels[2], color = "Compartment",
         shape = "Host genus", title = paste(distance_label, "ordination")) +
    theme(legend.position = "bottom")
}

p_bray <- plot_pcoa(bray_scores)
p_aitchison <- plot_pcoa(aitchison_scores)
p_bray / p_aitchison

ggsave(file.path(fig_dir, "AMF_PCoA_Bray_Aitchison.pdf"),
       p_bray / p_aitchison, width = 12, height = 13)
```

These global ordinations are descriptive because the host × compartment matrix
contains structural zeros. The primary tests below use only estimable subsets.

## 10.1 Prespecified, estimable PERMANOVA models

1. BR versus BS among the four host genera having both compartments, adjusted
   for host genus with an additive model.
2. Rh versus root among the three host genera having both compartments, adjusted
   for host genus with an additive model.
3. Within-host compartment tests, with independent samples and no blocking.

All tests are accompanied by PERMDISP. A significant PERMANOVA with significant
dispersion must not be described simply as a centroid/composition difference.
The shared-compartment models are additive because the primary estimand is the
overall compartment contrast after accounting for host. Host-specific tests
below are used to examine whether the pattern is consistent among hosts; the
small cell sizes do not support a reliable omnibus host-by-compartment
interaction test.

```{r permanova-functions}
subset_beta_data <- function(sample_ids) {
  x <- beta_rel[sample_ids, , drop = FALSE]
  x <- x[, colSums(x) > 0, drop = FALSE]
  list(
    x = x,
    d = vegdist(x, method = "bray"),
    meta = droplevels(meta_beta[sample_ids, , drop = FALSE])
  )
}

run_design_test <- function(label, sample_ids, formula_rhs, dispersion_group) {
  dat <- subset_beta_data(sample_ids)
  model_formula <- as.formula(paste("dat$d ~", formula_rhs))
  perm <- adonis2(model_formula, data = dat$meta, permutations = 999, by = "margin")

  group <- droplevels(factor(dat$meta[[dispersion_group]]))
  disp <- betadisper(dat$d, group)
  disp_test <- permutest(disp, permutations = 999)

  list(label = label, permanova = perm, dispersion = disp_test,
       distance = dat$d, metadata = dat$meta)
}
```

```{r permanova-primary}
soil_hosts <- c("Espeletia", "Chusquea", "Oritrophium", "Racomitrium")
soil_ids <- rownames(meta_beta)[
  meta_beta$Host_species %in% soil_hosts & meta_beta$Compartment %in% c("BR", "BS")
]

root_rh_hosts <- c("Chusquea", "Calamagrostis", "Oreobolus")
root_rh_ids <- rownames(meta_beta)[
  meta_beta$Host_species %in% root_rh_hosts & meta_beta$Compartment %in% c("Rh", "root")
]

test_soil <- run_design_test(
  "BR_vs_BS_across_four_hosts", soil_ids,
  "Host_species + Compartment", "Compartment"
)

test_root_rh <- run_design_test(
  "Rh_vs_root_across_three_hosts", root_rh_ids,
  "Host_species + Compartment", "Compartment"
)

test_soil$permanova
test_soil$dispersion
test_root_rh$permanova
test_root_rh$dispersion

capture.output(test_soil$permanova,
               file = file.path(table_dir, "PERMANOVA_BR_vs_BS.txt"))
capture.output(test_soil$dispersion,
               file = file.path(table_dir, "PERMDISP_BR_vs_BS.txt"))
capture.output(test_root_rh$permanova,
               file = file.path(table_dir, "PERMANOVA_Rh_vs_root.txt"))
capture.output(test_root_rh$dispersion,
               file = file.path(table_dir, "PERMDISP_Rh_vs_root.txt"))
```

```{r permanova-within-host}
within_host_tests <- lapply(levels(meta_beta$Host_species), function(host) {
  ids <- rownames(meta_beta)[meta_beta$Host_species == host]
  md <- droplevels(meta_beta[ids, , drop = FALSE])

  compartment_n <- table(md$Compartment)
  tested_parts <- names(compartment_n)[compartment_n >= 2]
  excluded_parts <- names(compartment_n)[compartment_n < 2]
  ids <- ids[meta_beta[ids, "Compartment"] %in% tested_parts]
  md <- droplevels(meta_beta[ids, , drop = FALSE])

  if (nrow(md) < 4 || nlevels(md$Compartment) < 2) {
    return(NULL)
  }

  dat <- subset_beta_data(ids)
  perm <- adonis2(dat$d ~ Compartment, data = dat$meta, permutations = 999)
  disp <- permutest(
    betadisper(dat$d, droplevels(dat$meta$Compartment)),
    permutations = 999
  )

  tibble(
    Host_species = host,
    n = nrow(md),
    compartments = nlevels(md$Compartment),
    tested_compartments = paste(levels(md$Compartment), collapse = "; "),
    excluded_singleton_compartments = if_else(
      length(excluded_parts) == 0,
      NA_character_,
      paste(excluded_parts, collapse = "; ")
    ),
    R2 = perm$R2[1],
    F = perm$F[1],
    p_PERMANOVA = perm$`Pr(>F)`[1],
    p_PERMDISP = disp$tab$`Pr(>F)`[1]
  )
}) %>%
  bind_rows() %>%
  mutate(q_PERMANOVA = p.adjust(p_PERMANOVA, method = "BH"))

within_host_tests
write.csv(within_host_tests, file.path(table_dir, "PERMANOVA_within_host.csv"),
          row.names = FALSE)
```

## 10.2 Pairwise within-host contrasts

```{r pairwise-permanova}
pairwise_permanova <- function(host) {
  ids_host <- rownames(meta_beta)[meta_beta$Host_species == host]
  groups <- droplevels(meta_beta[ids_host, "Compartment"])
  pairs <- combn(levels(groups), 2, simplify = FALSE)

  map_dfr(pairs, function(pair) {
    keep <- groups %in% pair
    ids <- ids_host[keep]
    dat <- subset_beta_data(ids)
    dat$meta$Compartment <- droplevels(dat$meta$Compartment)
    if (any(table(dat$meta$Compartment) < 2)) return(tibble())

    perm <- adonis2(dat$d ~ Compartment, data = dat$meta, permutations = 999)
    disp <- permutest(
      betadisper(dat$d, dat$meta$Compartment), permutations = 999
    )

    tibble(
      Host_species = host,
      contrast = paste(pair, collapse = " vs "),
      n = nrow(dat$meta),
      R2 = perm$R2[1],
      F = perm$F[1],
      p_PERMANOVA = perm$`Pr(>F)`[1],
      p_PERMDISP = disp$tab$`Pr(>F)`[1]
    )
  })
}

pairwise_results <- map_dfr(levels(meta_beta$Host_species), pairwise_permanova) %>%
  group_by(Host_species) %>%
  mutate(q_PERMANOVA = p.adjust(p_PERMANOVA, method = "BH")) %>%
  ungroup()

write.csv(pairwise_results,
          file.path(table_dir, "PERMANOVA_pairwise_within_host.csv"),
          row.names = FALSE)
pairwise_results
```

# 11. Differential abundance

Differential abundance is restricted to the same two balanced/shared comparisons
used above. Family-level aggregation is primary because phylogenetic family calls
are more defensible than interpreting thousands of AMF rDNA ASVs as species.
ANCOM-BC2 is optional because it is computationally intensive and should be run
only after reviewing the validated AMF depth/coverage diagnostics.

```{r ancombc2, eval=RUN_ANCOMBC2}
if (!requireNamespace("ANCOMBC", quietly = TRUE)) {
  stop("Install ANCOMBC before setting run_ancombc2: true.")
}

run_ancom_shared <- function(ps_input, hosts, parts, reference_part, label) {
  ps_sub <- subset_samples(
    ps_input,
    Host_species %in% hosts & Compartment %in% parts
  )
  ps_sub <- prune_taxa(taxa_sums(ps_sub) > 0, ps_sub)
  ps_sub <- tax_glom(ps_sub, taxrank = "Family", NArm = FALSE)

  sample_data(ps_sub)$Host_species <- droplevels(sample_data(ps_sub)$Host_species)
  sample_data(ps_sub)$Compartment <- relevel(
    droplevels(sample_data(ps_sub)$Compartment), ref = reference_part
  )

  result <- ANCOMBC::ancombc2(
    data = ps_sub,
    tax_level = NULL,
    fix_formula = "Host_species + Compartment",
    rand_formula = NULL,
    p_adj_method = "BH",
    pseudo_sens = TRUE,
    prv_cut = 0.10,
    lib_cut = 0,
    group = "Compartment",
    struc_zero = TRUE,
    neg_lb = TRUE,
    global = FALSE,
    pairwise = TRUE,
    dunnet = FALSE,
    trend = FALSE,
    n_cl = 1,
    verbose = TRUE
  )

  saveRDS(result, file.path(out_path, paste0("ANCOMBC2_", label, ".rds")))
  result
}

ancom_soil <- run_ancom_shared(
  ps_amf, soil_hosts, c("BR", "BS"), "BR", "BR_vs_BS"
)
ancom_root_rh <- run_ancom_shared(
  ps_amf, root_rh_hosts, c("Rh", "root"), "Rh", "Rh_vs_root"
)
```

# 12. Sensitivity analysis: ASVs versus 97% clusters

AMF can contain biologically real intragenomic LSU variants. Main community
composition is therefore reported at family/genus level, and richness claims must
be cautious. For a sensitivity analysis, cluster the validated AMF ASV sequences
at 97% identity with VSEARCH, sum counts by cluster, and repeat sections 7–10.
Do not call 97% clusters species; label them explicitly as 97% sequence clusters.

```{bash cluster-sensitivity, eval=FALSE}
set -euo pipefail

: "${AMF_CONDA_EXE:?Run the R paths chunk first}"
: "${AMF_CONDA_ENV:?Run the R paths chunk first}"
: "${LSU_PHYLO_DIR:?Run the R paths chunk first}"
cd "${LSU_PHYLO_DIR}"

"${AMF_CONDA_EXE}" run --no-capture-output -n "${AMF_CONDA_ENV}" vsearch \
  --cluster_size cladeOutputs/ASVrepseqs_clean_AMFonly.fasta \
  --id 0.97 \
  --strand plus \
  --centroids cladeOutputs/AMF_ASVs_97pct_centroids.fasta \
  --uc cladeOutputs/AMF_ASVs_97pct.uc
```

This clustering must be applied only to the phylogenetically validated AMF IDs
before count aggregation. The mapping is retained as supplementary provenance.

# Interpretation guardrails

- Do not use the prior 85% local-identity MaarjAM rule or any object derived from it.
- Do not merge BR and BS merely because a test is nonsignificant.
- Do not call ASVs or 97% clusters AMF species.
- Do not infer an ecosite effect unless independent sites/plots replicate ecosites
  separately from host identity.
- Do not use paired or repeated-measures statistics: the samples are independent.
- Report that LSU had no negative controls and that control-based contaminant
  identification could not be performed.
- Emphasize effect sizes, uncertainty, and dispersion diagnostics; n = 2–3 per
  host–compartment cell gives limited power.

<!-- Compartment: R²=0.19, p=0.001 — compartment explains 19% of AMF beta diversity -->
<!-- Host species: R²=0.23, p=0.001 — host explains 23%, slightly more than compartment -->
<!-- Full model (compartment × host): R²=0.60, p=0.001 — together they explain 60% of total variation, indicating strong joint structuring of AMF communities -->
<!-- Betadisper p=0.929 — dispersion is homogeneous across compartments, so the PERMANOVA result reflects true centroid differences, not just variance differences.  -->

<!-- AMF community composition differed significantly across plant compartments and host species. Variance partitioning of Bray-Curtis dissimilarities revealed that compartment and host species acted as independent predictors of AMF beta diversity, with negligible shared variance (−2.7%), indicating no collinearity between these factors in the experimental design. Compartment explained 16.7% of unique variance (dbRDA, F₄,₅₅ = 4.66, p = 0.001) and host species explained 18.8% (F₅,₅₅ = 4.35, p = 0.001), together accounting for 32.8% of total adjusted variation (full model F₉,₅₅ = 4.47, p = 0.001). Multivariate dispersion was homogeneous across compartments (betadisper, p = 0.929), confirming that compositional differences reflect true community turnover rather than differences in within-group variability. At the family level, ANCOM-BC2 identified Claroideoglomeraceae as significantly enriched in the endosphere relative to bulk soil (log-fold change = 2.07, Holm-corrected), consistent with the known root-colonizing preference of Claroideoglomus, while Ambisporaceae was significantly depleted in aboveground tissues (log-fold change = −3.51), reflecting its ecology as an obligate soil-dwelling lineage. -->

<!-- Significant findings: -->

<!-- Ambisporaceae significantly depleted in E_Aboveground vs bulk soil (lfc = −3.51, ~11× lower) — Ambispora are obligate soil/root colonizers with no aboveground function, so their absence aboveground is biologically expected and validates your data -->
<!-- Claroideoglomeraceae (Claroideoglomus) significantly enriched in D_Endosphere vs bulk soil (lfc = +2.07, ~8× higher) — this genus is a well-documented aggressive root colonizer, consistent with literature -->

<!-- Non-significant but notable trends in the LFC values: -->

<!-- Gigasporaceae lfc = +1.72 in endosphere, +1.48 aboveground — trends toward enrichment in plant-associated compartments but underpowered (n=3 replicates) -->
<!-- Diversisporaceae and Ambisporaceae both strongly negative in endosphere and aboveground — soil-preferring families -->
<!-- Paraglomeraceae lfc = −0.81 in root-affected soil — early depletion trend moving away from bulk -->

<!-- # Notes and Reminders -->

<!-- ## Key decisions made in this analysis: -->

<!-- 1. **maxEE = 2** retained 84.9% of reads — no need to relax threshold -->
<!-- 2. **Pooling**: default (no pooling) was sufficient given read depth -->
<!-- 3. **OTUs vs ASVs**: Analyses run at Family and Genus level via `tax_glom()`, -->
<!--    which collapses intra-genomic ASV variants — OTU clustering not required -->
<!-- 4. **Taxonomy**: MaarjAM LSU database (local BLAST, pident ≥ 85%) used in  -->
<!--    place of Delavaux phylogenetic placement. Recovered 3,318 AMF ASVs across -->
<!--    9 families. NCBI 28S_fungal used for non-AMF fungi classification. -->
<!-- 5. **Geosiphonaceae excluded** (421 ASVs) — not a plant-symbiotic AMF -->
<!-- 6. **Differential abundance**: ANCOM-BC2 at Family and Genus level -->
<!--    (compositional-aware). ASV-level underpowered at n=3 replicates/group. -->
<!-- 7. **Phylogenetic tree**: Not built — UniFrac not standard for AMF LSU; -->
<!--    Bray-Curtis used for all beta diversity -->

<!-- ## Files produced: -->
<!-- - `seqtab_nochim.rds` — ASV count table (4,631 ASVs, 65 samples) -->
<!-- - `read_tracking.rds` — reads through each pipeline step -->
<!-- - `ASVs.fasta` — ASV representative sequences -->
<!-- - `ASV_ID_mapping.csv` — maps ASV IDs to sequences -->
<!-- - `taxonomy_maarjam.rds` — final taxonomy table (MaarjAM + NCBI) -->
<!-- - `ps_amf.rds` — phyloseq object, AMF only (3,318 ASVs) -->
<!-- - `ANCOMBC2_family_LFC_heatmap.pdf` — differential abundance figure -->
<!-- - `AMF_family_relabund.pdf` — family composition by compartment -->
